headline: Atlases, spatial repositories and multimodal tools turn cell-level data into disease context
label: Spatial And Single Cell Reference
summary: New atlases, spatial repositories and perturbation benchmarks are being paired with neighborhood-aware tools for tumor annotation and clinical prediction.
synthesis: The dominant thread is consolidation of single-cell and spatial data into reusable references, with analysis layers that resolve cellular neighborhoods and disease states. PANGEA remaps 12.6M cells into a 32-type, 165-subtype hierarchy spanning 160 diseases. CROST 2.0 expands to 544 spatial transcriptomics projects with niche and cancer-niche tools, and CellStressDB indexes 131 physical-stress studies. Spatial methods emphasize neighborhoods: SPIN integrates spatially informed cell-type co-expression networks with Bayesian regression for population-scale clinical prediction, Sphinx models adaptive neighborhoods in spatial proteomics, and SpaceMACE combines CNV inference and spatial context to annotate tumor cells. In multi-omics, GatorAnchor refines cross-modal neighborhoods under uncertainty and scMINA prioritizes regulators from paired RNA–ATAC data. Loki2 decodes transcriptomic and protein signals from H&E at single-cell resolution. On the perturbation side, a benchmark of six drug-response transcriptomic resources finds limited cross-source concordance, while new PDO screens supply training data for drug response models.
